newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Eight NATO ships visit Moroccan city.
newsitem.headline: Eight NATO ships visit Moroccan city.

text.p: Eight NATO ships, with a total complement of 1,700 crew, docked on Thursday in the Moroccan port of Casablanca.
The North Atlantic Alliance Organisation fleet arrived for a six-day visit to Morocco, the first by a NATO fleet to the North African country, officials said.
The NATO force staff led by Captain Konstantinos Nikitiadis met Casablanca's Navy Base commander Belkacem Ait Moha and city governor Hamouda el Caid, they added.

The ships were part of the Standing Naval Force Mediterranean, which was inaugurated in 1992 when it replaced the NATO Naval On Call Force Mediterranean, a force available to the Supreme Allied Command in Europe since 1969.
Captain Nikitiadis described the forces' visit to Morocco as a get "to know and to be known" mission.
The fleet, comprised of Greek, German, Italian, Dutch, Spanish and American frigates, will leave next Tuesday for the Mediterranean island of Sicily.
